questions.cardDe: An wem wurden die bisher ältesten Tattoos entdeckt: Gletschermumie Ötzi, einer Chinchorro-Mumie oder König Tutanchamun?
questions.de: Welche rund 5300 Jahre alte Gletschermumie galt lange als ältester Fund eines Menschen mit Tätowierungen?
questions.en: Which glacier mummy, about 5,300 years old, was long considered the oldest find of a human with tattoos?

timeline.labelEn: Ötzi the Iceman dies in the Ötztal Alps, his skin bearing 61 tattoos
timeline.labelDe: Ötzi stirbt in den Ötztaler Alpen; seine Haut trägt 61 Tätowierungen

questions.notes: Multiple choice reworked. Ötzi (died 3368–3108 BC) holds the record for number of tattoos (61); in 2018 two Gebelein mummies from Egypt (up to 5,351 years old) were reported with possibly older, figurative tattoos, so the reworked question asks what was long considered the oldest. The Chinchorro tattoo dates to 2563–1972 BC; Tutankhamun is far younger.

questions.en: Which piece of technology, which once shaped the streetscape, was first installed in Germany in 1904 and will probably soon have disappeared completely?

timeline.labelEn: Wilhelm Quante develops the first telephone box in Germany
timeline.labelDe: Wilhelm Quante entwickelt die erste Telefonzelle in Deutschland

questions.notes: Card misprints „Deutschand“; only that typo is corrected in de (hence reworked). The 1904 date follows the source (Quante's booth); de.wikipedia (Telefonzelle (Deutschland)) dates the first public „Fernsprechkiosk“ in Berlin to 12 January 1881. Deutsche Telekom has been removing its remaining public phones.
